title: A House for the Harvest
premise: Zephyrine Ishikawa returns to the family farmhouse to bury her twin brother Zephyrus, only to discover the body in the casket is not him — and the house has been keeping him, or something wearing his face, alive inside its mirrors for twelve years. The house demands a harvest: a song passed down through their mother's line must be completed by a living voice, and every verse sung binds the singer closer to the walls. As Zephyrine pieces together her mother's forbidden last verse, she realizes the previous 'harvests' were her missing relatives, absorbed to feed the house's hunger for belonging. In the end, Zephyrine refuses to sing alone — instead she teaches the trapped souls, including her brother, to sing the final verse together, breaking the house's claim and freeing them, though she must remain as its reluctant keeper until it learns to be empty.
about_author: Petra Brightwater is the pen name of a former funeral home receptionist from coastal Oregon who writes horror about houses that love too much. Her work draws on family folklore and the quiet dread of inherited obligations.

chapters.title: The Wrong Body
chapters.summary: Zephyrine arrives at the Ishikawa farmhouse for the funeral and lifts the casket lid to find a stranger's face where her twin's should be. Told in her close third-person POV, the chapter establishes her guilt over twelve years away. Emotional beat: grief curdling into disbelief.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Flashback interwoven with present: young Zephyrine cataloguing the house's noises — footsteps upstairs, humming in the walls — while her mother insisted they were 'just the settling.' Present-day Zephyrine hears the humming again at the wake. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: dread reawakening.

chapters.title: The Mirror Runs Late
chapters.summary: Alone in the bathroom, Zephyrine notices her reflection lags a full second behind her movements. She tests it with deliberate gestures; the reflection eventually stops copying her entirely and simply watches. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: the first undeniable wrongness.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Won't Say
chapters.summary: Zephyrine visits elderly neighbor Odette Crane, who reveals the Ishikawa women have always 'fed' the house with a harvest song — and that her mother didn't die of illness but of finishing it. POV: Zephyrine with Odette's testimony. Beat: inheritance revealed as curse.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Hallway
chapters.summary: At night Zephyrine hears Zephyrus calling from the sealed east wing. Against every instinct she follows and finds a mirror standing free of any wall, his hand pressed against the glass from inside. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: hope weaponized.

chapters.title: My Brother's Second-Long Smile
chapters.summary: Through the mirror, Zephyrus communicates by writing backwards on the glass: DON'T SING THE LAST VERSE. He warns that the house lets the dead speak only to lure singers closer. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: love against warning.

chapters.title: Mother's Hymnal
chapters.summary: Searching the attic, Zephyrine finds her mother's hymnal with verses one through five annotated and the sixth torn out. The margins contain names — dozens — each crossed out on the date they vanished. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: scale of the horror lands.

chapters.title: Odette Remembers the Verse
chapters.summary: Odette confesses she heard the sixth verse once as a girl and has spent sixty years refusing to hum it. She agrees to teach Zephyrine everything except the ending. POV shifts partially to Odette. Beat: found family forming under threat.

chapters.title: The House Learns Her Name
chapters.summary: The house begins responding to Zephyrine directly: doors open before she touches them, warm meals appear, her childhood room restored. It is courting her. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: seduction of belonging — the most dangerous temptation.

chapters.title: Harvest Guests
chapters.summary: Zephyrine discovers the other trapped souls in the mirrors: aunts, a grandfather, children — generations harvested. They beg her not to free them, claiming the singing is peace. POV: Zephyrine among the glass crowd. Beat: ambiguity of comfort versus captivity.

chapters.title: Verse Five
chapters.summary: Testing herself, Zephyrine sings the fifth verse aloud to strengthen Zephyrus's presence in the glass. It works — he becomes nearly solid — but the house's walls begin breathing, and her own reflection starts mouthing words she isn't saying. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: power and cost entwined.

chapters.title: The Reflection's Argument
chapters.summary: Her lagging reflection speaks: it claims to be the part of her the house already owns, and argues that belonging here is better than the lonely years away. Zephyrine nearly believes it. POV: Zephyrine in dialogue with herself. Beat: internal climax of theme.

chapters.title: Odette's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Zephyrine finds Odette's cottage abandoned, teacup still warm, and a single line of the sixth verse penciled on the table — the house took her mid-lesson. Guilt and fury drive Zephyrine home to finish what Odette started. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: mentor lost, resolve hardened.

chapters.title: Inside the East Wing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine physically enters the mirror, crossing into the house's interior — an endless version of the farmhouse where harvested souls tend phantom fields. She finds Zephyrus and Odette both. POV: Zephyrine beyond the glass. Beat: commitment without return.

chapters.title: The Song That Feeds
chapters.summary: In the mirror-world, Zephyrine witnesses a harvest in progress: the house singing through the mouths of the dead, drawing a wandering drifter into the walls. She understands the mechanism — the song doesn't trap souls, hunger does; the song just opens the door. POV: Zephyrine observing. Beat: rules clarified, stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: What Zephyrus Did
chapters.summary: Zephyrus confesses: twelve years ago he tried to destroy the house by singing the sixth verse alone, and it took him mid-note — his failure created the lag in every mirror. He begged her not to repeat it. POV: Zephyrine listening. Beat: the truth reframes everything.

chapters.title: The House Makes Its Offer
chapters.summary: The house manifests as her mother's voice and offers Zephyrine everything: Zephyrus restored, Odette returned, a family that never leaves. All it asks is the last verse, sung willingly. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: lowest moment — the offer is almost perfect.

chapters.title: Learning the Last Verse
chapters.summary: Odette, half-dissolved into the mirror-world, gives Zephyrine the true sixth verse: it was never meant to be sung alone or to the house, but with others, for each other — a binding of people, not property. POV: Zephyrine learning. Beat: key turned in the lock.

chapters.title: Every Mirror in the House
chapters.summary: Zephyrine races back through the glass and moves mirror to mirror, waking each trapped soul and teaching them their line of the verse. The house fights back — slamming doors, flooding rooms, wearing faces. POV: Zephyrine under assault. Beat: rising action toward climax.

chapters.title: The Harvest Reversed
chapters.summary: Climax: in the great hall, Zephyrine and dozens of freed voices sing the complete song together, turning the house's hunger inward. Walls crack, mirrors shatter outward, and the harvested souls step free into moonlight — including Zephyrus, solid and weeping. POV: Zephyrine leading. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: An Empty House Learns Quiet
chapters.summary: The house, starved but not destroyed, shrinks into ordinary silence. Zephyrus and the others leave for lives interrupted decades ago; Odette chooses to stay nearby. Zephyrine feels the pull of the walls asking to be filled again. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: bittersweet aftermath.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Quiet
chapters.summary: Resolution: Zephyrine stays — not as prey but as keeper, teaching the house to want nothing, humming only fragments never completed. Final image: she waves goodbye to her brother from the porch, and for the first time, no mirror anywhere runs late. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: chosen belonging, on her terms.
